newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso soft on pre-election dlr short-cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso soft on pre-election dlr short-cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened slightly softer on Friday after dealers covered short dollar positions ahead of Sunday's mid-term elections, traders said.
Dealing was slow, however, as U.S. investors were out of the market due to the July 4 Independence Day holiday.
"Some locals are driving demand for dollars by squaring their books or even going long," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart opened 0.7 and 0.6 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9640/7.9680 and 7.9610/7.9650 per dollar.
Dealing in same-day peso contracts was suspended for the day due to the closure of U.S. financial markets.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.
Traders said the peso had also weakened due to the lack of dollars in the market.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9500/7.9700 per dollar for the 48-hour peso.
